newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Waste Management.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Big roll in Waste Management.

text.p: An investor rolled a sizable position in Waste Management Inc calls Tuesday, going from the soon-to-be-expired August 30 calls to the September 30 calls.
Ten thousand contracts of each traded. August options expire at the end of the week.
In afternoon activity, the stock was ahead 3/16 at 32-1/8.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co, said the investor bought the September 30 calls and sold the August 30 calls when the stock was trading at 32-1/16.
"It looks like a straight roll," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co. "It looks like the open interest is going from August to September."
The WMX August 30 call had open interest of 11,149 contracts through Monday while the September 30 call had open interest of just 1,050 contracts.
The August 30 call slipped 1/8 to two and the September 30 call gained 1/16 to 2-13/16.
In other activity, solid volume in some Boeing Co August calls was related to Friday's expiration.
The Boeing August 45 call traded 2,500 contracts, the August 47-1/2 call traded 2,760 and the August 50 call traded about 6,115.
Traders said the volume was investors closing out positions ahead of the expiration and not a dividend play.
Boeing shares, which were down 1-5/16 at 57-3/4 in afternoon trade, go ex-dividend Wednesday.

To take advantage of a dividend, investors sometimes buy deep-in-the-money calls and sell similar options as a hedge, then exercise the long position before the ex-date to collect the payout, hoping the shorts do not get exercised.
The Boeing August 45 call had 3,537 contracts open, the August 47-1/2 call had about 2,600 contracts open and the August 50 call had 8,420 contracts open.
Schwartz said he doubted the activity was dividend related because the cost would be high for a dividend payout of only $0.14 a share.

He said that in other trading, some action in three Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp calls on the American Stock Exchange could also be from investors moving out of the August series, but the volume did not add up.
The August 35 call traded about 4,035 contracts, the September 35 call traded 4,200 and the November 40 call traded a little more than 4,300.
Traders said much of the August and September 35 call volume were spreads done together but that the November 40 call volume was separate.
